singlePurpose: Translate content explicitly requested by the user into the user's chosen language: selected text, the article on the current page for bilingual reading, webpage regions, text in images, locally extracted PDF text, and optional experimental video captions.

permissions.contextMenus: Provide user-triggered translation commands for selected text, bilingual reading of the current article, page regions, images, PDF documents and optional video captions. Commands are available in the relevant context only.
permissions.storage: Store translation settings, language preferences, reading-page styles, user-created region rules, wording preferences chosen by the user, bring-your-own-provider API keys and extension session credentials locally. Session storage briefly holds the article detected for bilingual reading and is cleared when the browser closes; articles the user saves are kept in the extension's own IndexedDB. Nothing is synced through the browser account.
permissions.scripting: Inject the packaged translation interface when the user requests a translation (including the packaged article-detection script when the user chooses bilingual reading) and restore packaged content-script functionality after an extension update. Scripts read the requested content and render translation overlays; no remotely hosted executable code is injected.
permissions.activeTab: Access the active tab after an explicit extension action or keyboard command to obtain the selected text, open translation tools and authorize current-tab audio capture for optional video captions.
permissions.tabCapture: Capture audio from the current tab only when the user explicitly starts experimental video captions. This does not capture the microphone. Recognition is local when supported. Only if the user enables cloud recognition is audio sent to Edge's browser speech service (Microsoft Azure). Recognized text is translated with the chosen provider or hosted service. Capture stops when captions are stopped.
permissions.offscreen: Run a packaged offscreen document for the optional experimental video caption feature. The Manifest V3 service worker has no DOM or media APIs, so this document consumes the user-authorized tab audio stream and runs browser speech recognition. It is created with USER_MEDIA and does not display ads or execute remote code.
permissions.hostPermissions: Content scripts on ordinary websites render translation controls and apply the user's saved region rules. The extension reads content for translation when requested by the user, including the article text of the current page when the user chooses bilingual reading; it does not collect a browsing history. HTTPS connections to app.huaci.app provide accounts, trial credits and hosted translation. Provider requests go to the selected OpenAI, DeepSeek or DeepL API, or to a custom HTTPS endpoint explicitly configured by the user. Account synchronization scripts are restricted to the production account site and official website. Browser-protected pages remain inaccessible.

remoteCodeExplanation: All JavaScript, PDF parsing code, fonts and character maps used by the extension are bundled. Translation API responses are data and are not evaluated as executable code. Browser-managed speech recognition is a browser service, not downloaded extension code.

dataPractices.personalInformation: Account email and username; Google sign-in retains only the provider account identifier and verified email.
dataPractices.authenticationInformation: Extension sessions and provider API keys are handled as authentication credentials. Provider API keys stay in local extension storage and are sent only to the configured provider.
dataPractices.websiteContent: Requested text, images, extracted PDF text, the cleaned-up article text for bilingual reading, the paragraph and selection used for alternative wordings, relevant wording preferences, and recognized captions are processed for translation. Whole PDF files stay local. Saved articles and wording preferences stay in local extension storage. Audio is processed locally unless cloud recognition is explicitly enabled.
dataPractices.billingInformation: Creem processes payment details directly. The backend retains payment object identifiers, status, amounts, currency and billing country, not card numbers.
dataPractices.location: Hosted requests retain only the two-letter country code supplied by the network provider. Free-trial abuse prevention stores a one-way keyed hash of the network address rather than the address itself. No GPS, precise location or device fingerprinting.
dataPractices.usage: Request counts, character counts, credits, subscription and abuse-prevention records are needed to provide hosted translation. No advertising, tracking SDKs or device fingerprinting. Our backend does not retain original text, images or translations.
dataPractices.instruction: Match these facts to the exact category definitions shown in Partner Center. Do not select a no-data-collected declaration or state that every request goes directly to a third-party provider.

testingNotes:
Version 2.2.0. No payment or API key is needed to test.

REVIEW ACCOUNT (1,000 credits preloaded; expires {EXPIRES} UTC)
1. In the same Edge profile where the extension is installed, open https://app.huaci.app/review-login
2. Email: {EMAIL}
   Review access key: {ACCESS_KEY}
3. Click the extension toolbar icon > "Log in / Sign up" > approve the authorization. If the regular login page opens, change its address to /review-login in that tab; the authorization continues after sign-in.
Regular users sign in with an email verification code or Google; /review-login exists only for certification.

GUEST TRIAL (no sign-in)
On first install the extension requests trial credits from https://app.huaci.app and opens a welcome page. Trial credits are limited per network, so a shared test network may receive 0 credits. If so, use the review account above.

WHAT TO TEST (the default "credits" provider needs no setup)
- Open an ordinary article page (for example a news article) > right-click on an empty area without selecting text > "Read this article bilingually": a scan animation runs, then a reading page opens next to the tab with original and translation aligned paragraph by paragraph. Try the view switch, the light/dark button, "Save" (saved articles are listed on the right) and click a word in the translation to see alternative wordings.
- Select text on any webpage > right-click > "Translate to <language>": streamed result, show original, copy, Esc to close.
- Right-click an image containing text > "Translate text in image".
- Open a text-based PDF in Edge's built-in viewer > right-click > "Translate entire PDF". Only extracted text is sent; the file is not uploaded.
- Right-click a page area > "Add a translation button to this region".
- Settings: target language and interface language (24 languages, including right-to-left); shortcuts at edge://extensions/shortcuts.
- Log out from the extension or from https://app.huaci.app; both sides sign out in this browser.

NOT REQUIRED FOR TESTING
- Subscriptions: optional; plans are shown in the account center.
- Bring-your-own-key mode: needs the tester's own provider key.
- Video captions: experimental, off by default, depends on browser speech support.

Support: support@huaci.app
releaseNotes: Version 2.2.0: bilingual reading (detects the article on a page, strips navigation and ads, and opens a side-by-side reading page with light/dark appearance and local saving); click a word in a translation for alternative wordings, with local wording preferences applied to later translations; image translation outlines text along its strokes, keeps vertical CJK text vertical and lets users edit shapes before translating. The product is renamed Huaci – AI Translator & Bilingual Reader.
